task.title: storypole show --json nests the task under 'task' while other commands do not, which breaks naive consumers

acceptance_criteria: EVIDENCE 2026-11-06: 'storypole show GB-269 --json' has no top-level 'status' key because it nests the task under 'task'
while 'storypole list --json' returns a bare array. A python one-liner written against list broke on show with KeyError: 'status'. Proposed: one documented envelope for every --json command (or none)
stated in CONTRACTS.md so agent tooling can rely on it. Erring toward a stable envelope is worth more than a slightly shorter payload
because the consumers are scripts that cannot see a shape change.

DECISION 2026-11-06: adopt a single envelope everywhere rather than reconciling two commands. Best practice for CLI JSON is that the output is a CONTRACT - consumers are scripts that cannot see a shape change - and that an object beats a bare array because an array has nowhere to put anything added later (count
echoed filters
warnings
provenance). The current asymmetry is the symptom; the disease is that nothing states what --json emits
which is why list and show diverged.\n\nSHAPE
following the suite's snake_case convention everywhere else:\n  { 'schema_version': 1
'command': 'list'
'count': 42 }\n  { 'schema_version': 1
'command': 'show'
'decisions': [...] }\nPayload key names the thing
never 'data'. Do NOT add a second mode such as --json=payload: two modes recreate exactly the inconsistency being fixed.\n\nWHY NOW: the repository went public today with no external consumers
so this is the cheapest moment in the project's life for a breaking change; my own script broke on show --json with KeyError: 'status' today
so the failure mode is observed rather than theoretical; both commands can be reconciled in one commit while there are only two; and CH-10/GB-273 will consume this output
so building them first means coding against an undefined contract twice.\n\nMIGRATION: emit the envelope unconditionally
record it in CONTRACTS.md as the authoritative --json shape
note BREAKING in the CHANGELOG
and update any in-repo consumers in the same commit. If an external consumer ever needs the bare form
the right answer is schema_version bumping
not a flag.
events.title: One documented --json envelope for every storypole command, with schema_version

acceptance_criteria: STANDARD LANDED 2026-11-06 (common + CONTRACTS.md). The envelope is now defined once in gaugeblock_contracts::json - a wire contract belongs there for the same reason SpoolEntry does
because every binary emits it and no tool should own the definition. envelope() merges an object payload beside schema_version and command
nests a non-object payload under 'payload' rather than losing it

and returns the serialisation error instead of emitting a partial envelope (a consumer receiving envelope keys with no data would have to guess whether the command produced nothing). Three tests. CONTRACTS.md gains a JSON envelope section stating the four rules and
deliberately

that a binary emitting JSON in another shape is a contract violation rather than a style choice.

Per the beta ruling: schema_version stays 1 for the whole 0.1.x line - bump only when a consumer must change.

REMAINING: adopt it in storypole's 19 emit sites
starting with list and show
then other binaries as they are touched. No in-repo consumer parses storypole --json (outfeed/storypole.rs has no JSON deserialisation)
so the break is contained to our own scripts - including the one that failed today with KeyError: 'status'.

ADOPTION INVENTORY 2026-11-06, so the sweep starts from a list rather than a grep. 19 JSON emit sites across 7 handler files in storypole-cli:

  core_cmds.rs        8
  plan_cmds.rs        3
  ledger_cmds.rs      2
  lifecycle_cmds.rs   2
  workspace_cmds.rs   2
  spool_cmds.rs       1
  update_cmd.rs       1

Order: list and show first (they are the documented examples and the ones my own scripts consume), then the mutating commands whose current output is a hand-written success object - those are also the ones that would benefit most from command and schema_version being present when reading a log back.

Do it in ONE commit with the CHANGELOG entry. Half-adopting the envelope while CONTRACTS.md asserts the standard is worse than the state before the ticket, because the document would then be wrong rather than merely absent.

ADOPTED 2026-11-06 (storypole commit). All 19 emit sites across 7 handler files route through json_out::print_json, which wraps gaugeblock_contracts::json::envelope. Verified end to end: list --json returns {command, count, schema_version, tasks} and show --json returns {briefing, command, schema_version}, both with schema_version 1. Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, 55/55.

Payload naming chosen per command rather than a generic 'data': tasks carries a count beside it, briefing stays whole, plan and receipt keep their own names - naming is what makes the output extensible without the next break.

Two build fixes paid along the way, both dependency declarations the CLI was getting transitively: gaugeblock-contracts (the envelope itself) and serde (the Serialize bound). Worth noting because it is the same class as the earlier TRANSPORT of types through benchwork-core - explicit edges are cheaper than transitive luck.
